The test image shows corn leaves with multiple small, round, raised yellowish-white bump/gall-like structures on the leaf surface. Key observations:
- Small, spherical/dome-shaped raised structures
- Pale yellow to white coloration
- Multiple scattered on the leaf blade
- No brown/tan lesion pattern, no rust-colored pustules

Top candidates: Common_smut (leaf galls), Common_rust (early pustules), Southern_rust. Let me check reference images.
The test structures are small, pale yellowish-white dome-shaped galls on leaf tissue — different from rust (reddish) or large smut galls. Let me check more references.

None of those match. The test image has raised, dome-shaped, fleshy yellowish-white galls — not flat spots. This strongly points to Common_smut (early-stage leaf galls). Let me view a few more references to confirm.
None of those match either. Let me view a few more to meet the minimum 12 reference images.

All 13 reference images reviewed confirm no other class produces raised, 3D fleshy dome-shaped galls like what appears in the test image.

**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image:** Corn leaf with multiple small (5-15mm), raised, dome-shaped, fleshy yellowish-white galls on the leaf surface. Structures are clearly 3-dimensional protrusions from leaf tissue.
- **Key distinguishing feature:** These are raised galls, not flat lesions, pustules, or spots.
- **Common_smut match:** The symptom description explicitly states galls "can appear on any above ground plant part at any time during the growing season" and "are initially white to gray and fleshy" — perfectly matching the yellowish-white fleshy domes on this leaf.
- **Ruled out:**
  - Rust diseases (Common_rust, Southern_rust) → brick-red/orange powdery pustules, not white fleshy domes
  - Tar_spot → black raised stromata, not white
  - Eyespot, Holcus_spot, Gray_leaf_spot, NCLB → all flat lesions
  - Head_smut → black spore masses in tassel/ear, not leaf galls
  - All other classes → wrong morphology entirely
